title: Route Distance Percentage Calculator
description: Turn distance covered into a progress percentage with the Route Distance Percentage Calculator — how far along, and how much remains. Free.
summary_sentence: For example, 465 miles into a 1,240-mile route is 37.5% done with 775 miles remaining — the two numbers every 'are we nearly there?' is really asking for.
quick_answer: The Route Distance Percentage Calculator divides the distance you have covered by the route's total distance and returns your progress as a percentage, with the distance remaining beside it. Enter both — from an odometer, a route plan or a trail log — and read how far along you are.

faq: What does this tool calculate?
Progress percentage: distance covered ÷ total route distance × 100, with the remaining distance reported alongside.
Is the result exact?
The division is exact; the meaning depends on honest inputs — odometer miles against the route's true total.
Do I need an account?
No. Two distances in, a percentage out.
Does the route include live traffic?
No. Progress by distance is gloriously indifferent to traffic — which is its morale advantage over time-based estimates.
Why is road distance longer than straight-line?
Use the route's road total as the denominator, or the percentage reaches 100 somewhere short of the destination.
Can I track by time instead?
Time percentage lies on uneven routes — the mountain half takes longer. Distance is the stable denominator; that is this tool's whole argument.
What if I have covered more than the total?
Then the route was longer than planned — update the total to the real one and the percentage becomes honest again. It happens to every honest traveller.
Halfway by distance but not by day?
Normal on uneven routes — the remaining half may hold the mountains. Percentage is a progress truth, not a time promise.
Can I use it for a swim or a channel row?
Distance is distance: covered over total, in any medium where you can measure both.
The kids ask every ten minutes.
Give them the percentage and the remaining miles together — one for hope, one for honesty. It works on adults too.
